chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a man who marries his son to an orphan girl under his care, while his son is mature and the orphan girl is not yet mature, he said: “Her marriage is valid for his son. Then if he dies, her inheritance from him is set aside until she reaches maturity. When she reaches maturity, she is made to swear by Allah that nothing prompted her to take the inheritance except her acceptance of the marriage. Then the inheritance and half of the dowry are given to her.”

He said: “But if she dies before reaching maturity and before the husband dies, the husband does not inherit from her, because she has the option regarding him once she reaches maturity, while he has no option regarding her.”

key_terms.الْخِيَارَ: the legal option to affirm or reject the marriage upon maturity
key_terms.رِضَاهَا بِالنِّكَاحِ: her acceptance and approval of the marriage
key_terms.يَتِيمَةً فِي حَجْرِهِ: an orphan girl under his guardianship and care

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance and dowry when a minor orphan girl is married by her guardian and one spouse dies before she reaches maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a fiqh ruling about the marriage of a mature son to a minor orphan girl under guardianship, and explains how inheritance and mahr are handled if death occurs before her maturity. It establishes that her later acceptance is legally significant, and that the husband does not inherit from her before that option is realized, because the right of choice belongs to her alone.
